answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital into a cryptographic vault to earn voting power. This economic barrier functions like a harsh tundra, freezing out unauthorized nodes lacking sufficient stake. The consensus kernel validates these financial commitments, ensuring that scaling the network requires tangible asset expenditure. An attacker must acquire a majority of total supply, imposing prohibitive costs that render large-scale identity spoofing mathematically irrational.
